title: 「One thing ... is ...」突出一項重點

formula: One thing + defining clause + is / was + complement

formulas.formula: One thing + defining clause + is / was + complement

example: One thing we cannot ignore is the cost of delay.
exampleZh: 我們不能忽視的一件事，是延誤的代價。

examples.en: One thing we cannot ignore is the cost of delay.
examples.zh: 我們不能忽視的一件事，是延誤的代價。
examples.highlight: One thing we cannot ignore is the cost of delay.

meaning.zh: 本課練習目標句型：One thing + defining clause + is / was + complement。

rules.zh: 中間部分用來限定 one thing 所指的是甚麼 （我們需要討論的一件事，是預算。） 中間的 we need to discuss 說明是哪一件事。
rules.en: The middle clause defines which one thing is meant. In “One thing we need to discuss is the budget”, we need to discuss identifies the particular thing.
examples: One thing we need to discuss is the budget.

rules.zh: 當 thing 是中間子句的受詞時，that 通常可以省略 以下兩句均正確： 在日常英語中，省略 that 的版本較常見。
rules.en: When thing is the object of the middle clause, that can normally be omitted. Both are correct: One thing that we should remember is the deadline. One thing we should remember is the deadline. The version without that is more common in everyday English.
examples: One thing that we should remember is the deadline.
One thing we should remember is the deadline.

rules.zh: 當 thing 是中間子句的主詞時，that 不可省略 正確： 錯誤： 因為是那件事情「令居民擔心」，所以 that 是子句的主詞，不可刪去。
rules.en: When thing is the subject of the middle clause, that cannot be omitted. Correct: One thing that concerns residents is the lack of buses. Incorrect: One thing concerns residents is the lack of buses. Here, that is the subject of concerns because the thing itself concerns residents.
examples: One thing that concerns residents is the lack of buses.
One thing concerns residents is the lack of buses.

rules.zh: 按照時間使用 is 或 was 現在情況： 過去情況：
rules.en: Choose is or was according to time. Present situation: One thing I enjoy is the flexible schedule. Past situation: One thing I noticed was how quiet the room was.
examples: One thing I enjoy is the flexible schedule.
One thing I noticed was how quiet the room was.

rules.zh: is／was 後面可以接不同內容 名詞或名詞詞組 that 子句 疑問詞子句 行動 當中間部分含有 do 時，後面通常使用原形動詞：
rules.en: Different complements can follow is or was: a noun or noun phrase, as in “One thing the room lacks is natural light”; a that-clause, as in “One thing we know is that regular sleep improves concentration”; a wh-clause, as in “One thing we need to discuss is how the plan will be funded”; or an action, as in “One thing you can do is ask the teacher for help.” When the middle clause contains do, the complement normally uses the base verb: One thing we should do is reduce waste.
examples: One thing the room lacks is natural light.
One thing we know is that regular sleep improves concentration.
One thing we need to discuss is how the plan will be funded.
One thing you can do is ask the teacher for help.
One thing we should do is reduce waste.

rules.zh: 不要與 The thing is, ... 混淆 指出某一項具體重點： 是一個談話用語，用來引出解釋、困難或真正情況： 兩者的結構和用途並不相同。
rules.en: Do not confuse “One thing ... is ...” with “The thing is, ....” The first identifies one specific point: One thing we need to change is the timetable. The second is a conversational expression introducing an explanation, difficulty or real situation: The thing is, we do not have enough time. Their structures and purposes differ.
examples: One thing we need to change is the timetable.
The thing is, we do not have enough time.

benefits.zh: 把讀者的注意力集中在一項重點上 當一個話題包含很多資料時，這個句型能告訴讀者：「以下這一點值得留意。」 讀者會立即知道句子的重點是 the cost of delay。
benefits.en: It focuses the reader on one important point. When a topic contains much information, the frame signals that the next point deserves attention. In “One thing we cannot ignore is the cost of delay”, the reader immediately recognises the cost of delay as the focus.

benefits.zh: 幫助你逐點組織內容 在作文、報告、會議或口頭回答中，你可以逐一提出不同重點： 這樣能避免把所有資料擠在同一句中，令說明更有條理。
benefits.en: It helps organise information point by point in essays, reports, meetings and spoken answers: One thing we need to consider is the cost. Another thing we need to consider is the time required. This avoids crowding all the information into one sentence.

benefits.zh: 把兩句短句合併成一句 比較： 改寫為： 第二個版本較緊湊，而且能清楚顯示「需要討論」與「預算」之間的關係。
benefits.en: It combines two short sentences into one. Compare: We need to discuss several matters. The budget is one of them. → One thing we need to discuss is the budget. The second version is tighter and clearly connects what needs discussion with the budget.

benefits.zh: 讓重點更加準確 中間部分可以說明為甚麼該項事情值得提出： 這不只是說「巴士不足」，而是準確說明這是令居民擔心的事情。
benefits.en: It makes the focus more precise because the middle clause can explain why the point matters: One thing that concerns residents is the lack of late-night buses. This identifies the bus shortage specifically as a concern, not merely as a fact.

benefits.zh: 避免重複使用 There is 或 It is important 學生經常寫： 你可以改用： 這能增加句式變化，令說話和寫作不會過分重複。
benefits.en: It avoids repeatedly using There is or It is important. Instead of “It is important to remember the deadline”, “It is important to consider the cost” and “It is important to check the details”, write: One thing we should remember is the deadline. One thing we should consider is the cost. One thing we should check is the details. This adds sentence variety.

benefits.zh: 提供容易使用的口語框架 在說話時，你可以先使用以下框架，再填入自己的內容： 這個框架能幫助你一邊思考，一邊有條理地表達答案。
benefits.en: It provides easy speaking frames: One thing I like about ___ is ___. One thing we need to improve is ___. One thing that concerns me is ___. One thing I learnt from this experience is ___. Fill in the blanks to organise an answer while you think.
